name: stream-cipher-corpus
description: Tests recall of stream cipher concepts including keystreams, linear feedback shift registers, XOR operations, self-synchronizing ciphers, and seed values.
sentence_templates: A {1} initialized with a {4} generates a {0} whose bits are combined with plaintext using a {2}, unlike a {3} which derives state from prior ciphertext.
The {2} combines each plaintext bit with a {0} bit derived from a {1} seeded by the {4}, while a {3} can recover sync automatically.
In a {3}, losing sync is self-correcting, whereas a synchronous cipher relying on a {1} and {4} must regenerate the entire {0} and reapply the {2}.
Security of the {0} depends on the {4} remaining secret and the {1} being nonlinear enough that the {2} output cannot be predicted, even by a {3} attacker.
The {4} initializes the {1}, which produces the {0}, combined via {2} with plaintext; a {3} additionally feeds ciphertext back to maintain synchronization.
